audit_items.proof_trace: BPO fork epochs from blob_schedule (config.rs:165) are not tracked by fork_context.next_fork(), which only tracks phase-based forks. When a blob schedule BPO fork is scheduled, the else branch (L623) correctly sets next_fork_version to current version, but L635-638 queries fork_context.next_fork() which returns None for BPO forks, causing next_fork_epoch to be FAR_FUTURE_EPOCH instead of the actual BPO fork epoch from blob_schedule.
audit_items.attack_scenario: A network schedules a BPO fork (blob limit change) at epoch E via blob_schedule. Peers advertise next_fork_epoch=FAR_FUTURE_EPOCH in ENR instead of epoch E. This causes peer discovery issues: nodes won't recognize each other as being on the same fork schedule, leading to network partitioning around the BPO fork activation.
